questions.text: According to PD 1067 (Water Code of the Philippines), Article 51, what public-use easement applies along the SHORES of the SEA in AGRICULTURAL areas?

options.text: 3 meters
20 meters
40 meters
75 meters

rationale.a: Wrong. 3 meters is the PD 1067 Article 51 easement in URBAN areas, not agricultural.
rationale.b: Correct. PD 1067 Article 51 establishes a 20-meter public-use easement in AGRICULTURAL areas along banks of rivers/streams and shores of seas/lakes.
rationale.c: Wrong. 40 meters is the PD 1067 Article 51 easement in FOREST areas, not agricultural. The figure is set by land classification, not by a uniform no-build zone.
rationale.d: Wrong. 75 meters is not a PD 1067 easement figure.
rationale.correct: PD 1067 Article 51: easement of public use along banks of rivers/streams and shores of seas/lakes is 3 m (urban), 20 m (agricultural), or 40 m (forest). For agricultural shores the easement is 20 meters.
rationale.takeaway: PD 1067 easements are determined by LAND CLASSIFICATION (urban/agricultural/forest), not by water-body width or a uniform coastal no-build zone.

questions.text: Which of the following is a required safeguard under RA 7279 when evicting or demolishing shelters occupied by underprivileged and homeless citizens?

options.text: At least thirty (30) days written notice, consultation on resettlement, presence of local government officials, and adequate relocation (temporary or permanent).
Verbal notice 24 hours before demolition with no obligation to consult or resettle.
A mayor's permit alone is sufficient to demolish without notice or relocation.
Immediate demolition is allowed whenever occupants are in a danger area, with no notice or relocation duty.

rationale.a: Correct. RA 7279 Section 28 lists the safeguards for eviction/demolition involving underprivileged and homeless citizens: at least 30 days notice, consultation on resettlement, presence of local government officials, proper identification of demolition personnel, regular office hours and good weather (unless families consent otherwise), limits on heavy equipment, proper police uniforms, and adequate relocation whether temporary or permanent.
rationale.b: Wrong. RA 7279 requires written notice of at least 30 days and consultation on resettlement, not 24-hour verbal notice.
rationale.c: Wrong. A mayor's permit alone is not a basis under RA 7279; lawful eviction requires one of the statutory grounds and the Section 28 safeguards.
rationale.d: Wrong. Danger-area occupancy is a basis for lawful eviction, but Section 28 safeguards (notice, etc.) and Section 29 relocation duties still apply.
rationale.correct: RA 7279 Section 28 enumerates the safeguards: 30-day notice, consultation on resettlement, presence of LGU officials, proper identification, regular hours/good weather, limits on heavy equipment, proper police uniforms, and adequate relocation.
rationale.takeaway: Even danger-area evictions under RA 7279 must follow Section 28 procedural safeguards and the Section 29 relocation duty.

questions.text: Under RA 7279, what must an adequate resettlement site provide, in addition to the physical relocation of occupants?

options.text: A minimum floor area of 24 sq m per family, with no other legal requirement
Basic services and facilities plus access to employment and livelihood opportunities
Free private transportation for life for all relocated families
Cash compensation equal to the appraised value of the previously occupied land

rationale.a: Wrong. The '24 sq m' floor-area figure is not in RA 7279 and was a fabricated detail in the original question. RA 7279 frames adequacy by basic services and livelihood access, not by a single floor-area number.
rationale.b: Correct. RA 7279 (article body) states LGUs, with the NHA, must provide relocation/resettlement sites with basic services and facilities plus access to employment and livelihood opportunities. This is the source-safe definition of adequacy.
rationale.c: Wrong. RA 7279 does not provide a lifetime free-transportation guarantee.
rationale.d: Wrong. RA 7279 does not grant cash compensation equal to land value to occupants of danger areas.
rationale.correct: RA 7279: resettlement sites must provide basic services and facilities and access to employment and livelihood. The statute does not specify a single floor-area figure for resettlement adequacy.
rationale.takeaway: Do not import a '24 sq m' floor-area figure into RA 7279 resettlement questions. Source-safe adequacy = basic services + livelihood access.

questions.text: Occupants of an informal settlement along an estero (a danger area listed under RA 7279) are threatened with eviction. What does RA 7279 require of the LGU and NHA regarding these occupants?

options.text: The LGU, with the NHA, must implement relocation and resettlement with basic services and access to employment or livelihood; even danger-area occupants retain RA 7279 safeguards such as notice and adequate relocation.
Danger-area occupants lose all RA 7279 rights and can be evicted immediately without notice or relocation.
Relocation is required only for occupants of privately owned land; danger-area occupants must self-relocate.
Relocation may be waived for danger-area occupants provided the LGU pays cash compensation in lieu of a resettlement site.

rationale.a: Correct. RA 7279 Section 29 directs LGUs, with the NHA, to implement relocation and resettlement of persons living in danger areas and to provide relocation/resettlement sites with basic services and facilities plus access to employment and livelihood. Section 28 procedural safeguards (notice, consultation, etc.) apply even in danger-area evictions.
rationale.b: Wrong. Danger-area occupancy does not strip occupants of all RA 7279 protections. The law lists danger areas as one basis for lawful eviction, but procedural safeguards and the government relocation obligation still apply.
rationale.c: Wrong. RA 7279 relocation duties apply broadly; they are not limited to private-land occupants.
rationale.d: Wrong. Cash compensation in lieu of a resettlement site is not authorized by RA 7279. The statute requires an adequate relocation/resettlement site.
rationale.correct: RA 7279 Section 29 (with Section 28): danger-area occupants retain the right to notice and to government-provided relocation. The LGU and NHA must implement relocation and resettlement with basic services and access to livelihood.
rationale.takeaway: Danger-area listing under RA 7279 permits eviction but does NOT waive the government's relocation duty or the Section 28 procedural safeguards.
